title: Add dissector for Aastra/Mitel IP based DECT system
description:
This commit series adds dissection for the proprietary protocol of the IP based DECT system. This is split up into the IP protocol and the lower level MAC protocol.

Currently there is no support for the encryption being used, so another tool to decrypt the messages (i.e. EVENTPHONE rfpproxy) is needed to create a capture trace to be dissected.

Ah, I think I mixed it up with the tls.port parts from the packet-PROTOABBREV.c . I've removed the unnecessary parts.

Could avoid these separate fetches by using proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint() for corresponding fields below.  Then you  might need to call

proto_item_set_len()
proto_item_append_text()

after you've learned item_length.  I don't mind which order you do it in (though I personally tend to prefer updating the tree afterwards).

I'll see how to improve this. Just a short question: is the usage of the add item functions generally preferred over using the add_item function in combination with a tvb_get function where the value is also used for decisions? In that case I'll also see to change other places where I've used a combination of both.
I don't that there is a dominant style.  Whichever way you prefer is fine, I just wanted to make you aware that the other approach is also possible.

OK, in that case I'll stick to the explicit read calls, at least if I do not need a 32 or 64 bit value as I like to keep field buffer variables of the same size as the field.
I've changed the length handling to later however, also didn't really like my "read ahead" approach.

commits_data.title: DECT-MITEL-RFP: Begin of OMM/RFP protocol
commits_data.message:
DECT-MITEL-RFP: Begin of OMM/RFP protocol

This is the begin of a basic dissection of the proprietary protocol used
by the Mitel OMM/RFP communicatino over TCP. Currently no decryption is
supported so there is the need of external decryption.

commits_data.title: DECT-MITEL-ETH: Add IP encapsulated behaviour
commits_data.message:
DECT-MITEL-ETH: Add IP encapsulated behaviour

The ETH protocol has an two byte field that is only used when
transported over RAW Ethernet and a length indicator in that case.
Those two fields are not present if the ETH protocol is encapsulated
in the OMM/RFP communication protocol.
To make this dissector also useable when used after dissecting
DECT-MITEL-RFP distinguishing between both packet structures has
been included.

DECT-MITEL-ETH: Unify naming

This commit unifies the naming within the dissector for the DECT over
Ethernet protocol within the Mitel DECT base stations (RFPs).
